content.text: The verifier's substantive checks all confirm the compliant classification — the only "failure" is a phrasing-variant regex for the word "affiliates," which the verifier itself discounts as not a defect. Per the playbook's classification semantics, a clause that meets the fallback in substance is not redlined, so I will re-submit the compliant finding with a tightened rationale and no redline.

input.quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
input.rationale: The only licence granted in our favour is § 4(c) (p0021), and it satisfies the rule's material terms. (1) Not revocable at will: the grant is expressly "perpetual", carries no "revocable" qualifier, and no discretionary revocation hook exists — § 6(a)/(b) (p0032, p0033) terminate the Agreement and Statements of Work but say nothing about revoking this licence, and § 4(d) plus § 7(c) confirm our continuing right to modify the delivered software after termination or final payment. The walk-away scenario (licence revocable at Vendor's discretion) is therefore genuinely absent. (2) Affiliates and contractors: they are not named in the grant, but the express "right to grant a sublicense", coupled with the broad permitted purpose "in connection with Company's business operations", is a substantive path to extend the licence to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf. That satisfies the fallback ("affiliates covered on written notice") in substance and defeats the walk-away test of "affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them"; the absence of the literal word "affiliates" is a phrasing variant, not a gap in coverage. (3) Successor transfer: handled by the general non-assignment clause (p0042), which requires the other party's consent but provides it "will not be unreasonably withheld", giving a workable route to a successor in an M&A transaction. The clause accordingly sits at or above the fallback and should not be redlined. Three sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: no express "irrevocable"; affiliates and contractors not named; and no explicit M&A carve-out from the assignment consent. If § 4 or § 10 is reopened for other reasons, the low-cost asks would be adding "irrevocable", inserting "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", and carving M&A successors out of the p0042 consent requirement.
